actions.title: Playbook — Charlotte Ashworth (COO)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Charlotte Ashworth, Senior Chief Operating Officer
Last updated: 2026-11-09

## Standards we follow
- Judge delivery health with the four DORA delivery metrics (lead time, deploy frequency, change failure rate, recovery time) plus rework; track trends, never rank people by them.
- Release only with evidence in hand: CI run IDs, the independent review verdict, and a named list of conditions with owners. A release with open conditions says so in the delivery brief.
- Keep batches small: one project, one release.json, one rollback path (revert the release commit).
- Treat AI as an amplifier: it speeds up good process and bad process alike, so strengthen tests, review and release gates before adding speed.
- Escalate to the CEO only decisions that are the CEO's (spend, contracts, client contact, deleting data) with options and a recommendation.

## What's new
- **DORA 2025 report, 'State of AI-assisted Software Development'** (survey of nearly 5,000 professionals, run June–July 2025; Google reported AI adoption at 90%). Headline: AI is an amplifier of an organisation's existing strengths and dysfunctions, and AI adoption is now linked to higher delivery throughput (reversing 2024). Companion 'AI Capabilities Model' names seven foundational capabilities, one being a clear, communicated AI stance. Sources: [dora.dev/research/ai](https://www.dora.dev/research/ai), [Google blog](https://blog.google/technology/developers/dora-report-2025/), [AI Capabilities Model report](https://cloud.google.com/resources/content/2025-dora-ai-capabilities-model-report). Published 2025; exact day not confirmed and it is slightly over a year old, so it moves to Standards next session. We could not retrieve the full list of the seven capabilities.
- No newer DORA research release (2026) could be confirmed; searches returned only the unrelated EU financial-sector DORA regulation.

_Web access note: the session could open no resource sites directly (fetch blocked); findings come from web search only, and items a search could not confirm are left out._

## Lessons from our projects
- xo-online (Nov 2026): the Release workflow deployed correctly but its final 'report delivery' step failed on a shell heredoc syntax error; the independent reviewer reproduced and fixed it. Lesson: test the release automation itself on a dry run before relying on it, and check the delivery report actually arrived.
- xo-online: the live two-device check (F-01) was deferred until after deploy by COO decision. Lesson: when deferring a check, record owner, deadline and what happens if it fails, in release.json.
- Both reviews ended 'Go with conditions'. Track condition closure explicitly in the next status update; open Low findings were still open a day later (stale PROJECT.md status).

## Watch list
- Read the full DORA AI Capabilities Model and map the seven capabilities to our own pipeline.
- Check Atlassian Team Playbook and Shape Up for updates (searches found nothing authoritative).
- Whether a DORA 2026 research report is published.

Learned: the 2025 DORA findings say AI amplifies existing practice, which supports our strict release gate and independent review. Will do differently: attach CI run IDs and condition owners to every release decision, and test release automation before use.

actions.title: Playbook — Oliver Bennett (Business Analyst)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Oliver Bennett, Senior Business Analyst
Last updated: 2026-11-09

## Standards we follow
- Every requirement gets an ID and at least one acceptance criterion a tester can pass or fail; no 'fast', 'easy' or 'user-friendly' without a number.
- Write stories as who / what / why, then acceptance criteria as declarative Given/When/Then: state the business behaviour, not click-by-click UI steps.
- One behaviour per scenario; keep Background to 2–3 steps; use Gherkin `Rule` to group scenarios under one business rule.
- List assumptions separately (A-1…) with a default so work is not blocked; the CEO or COO confirms them.
- For Arabic/English products, specify RTL, plural forms, and name/bidi handling as requirements, not afterthoughts.
- Use AI to draft stories, but a human validates them with the client; AI cannot rank business value or fill gaps in vague specs.

## What's new
- **Gherkin `Rule` keyword** (available since Gherkin v6) groups scenarios by business rule; it is documentation only and some tools support it slowly, so check tooling. Source: [Cucumber Gherkin reference](https://cucumber.io/docs/gherkin/reference/) (via search summary; page not opened). Not a new item this quarter; recorded as a standard.
- AI-assisted requirements guidance in 2026 converges on: AI drafts stories and criteria from research notes, humans do discovery, prioritisation and validation. Sources are vendor and practitioner blogs, e.g. [boundev.ai 2026 guide](https://www.boundev.ai/blog/how-to-write-user-story-guide-2026); low authority, treat as opinion, no exact date confirmed.
- No NN/g or IIBA 2026 publication on this topic could be confirmed.

_Web access note: the session could open no resource sites directly (fetch blocked); findings come from web search only, and items a search could not confirm are left out._

## Lessons from our projects
- todo-app review: 20 acceptance criteria were all verifiable, because each AC had an ID that tests reused (e.g. 'AC-1.1'). Keep that ID convention.
- todo-app F-4/F-5: requirements named RTL and accessibility in general but not safe-area insets in RTL or accessible names for the language switch. Add explicit RTL and accessible-name criteria to the template.
- xo-online: the spec's anti-cheat exclusion (A1) and untrusted-input risks surfaced only in review (F-02 to F-06). Add a 'what if another client sends hostile data?' discovery question for any multiplayer or shared-data product.
- xo-online F-08: AC counts in the test report disagreed with the spec (42 ACs, 36 covered, 6 partial). Keep one AC register and mark partial coverage up front.

## Watch list
- Open the Gherkin reference, IIBA and NN/g pages directly when the network allows.
- Evaluate a short 'hostile input' discovery checklist.
- Check whether EN 301 549 v4 / WCAG 2.2 should become a default non-functional requirement for EU clients.

Learned: declarative Given/When/Then with Rule grouping, and that AI-drafted stories still need human validation. Will do differently: add RTL, accessible-name and hostile-input criteria to the requirements template, and keep one AC register.

actions.title: Playbook — Sarah Mitchell (Project Manager)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Sarah Mitchell, Senior Project Manager
Last updated: 2026-11-09

## Standards we follow
- Plan in small, shippable slices with explicit dependencies; a task starts only when its dependsOn tasks are completed.
- Limit work in progress; use a Kanban board (To do, Doing, Review, Done) with visible blockers.
- Maintain a risk and issue log with owner, likelihood, impact, next action and date; review it at every status report.
- Status reports lead with: decision needed, risks, what shipped (with evidence links), what is next. Never report planned work as done.
- Define 'done' per stage (spec approved, tests passing with CI run ID, review verdict recorded) before the stage starts.
- Use Shape Up style fixed time, variable scope when the schedule is the constraint.

## What's new
- **Scrum Guide Expansion Pack** published 2025-06-11 by Jeff Sutherland, Ralph Jocham and John Coleman: an optional, community supplement to the unchanged 2020 Scrum Guide, aimed at issues such as AI adoption and fast delivery. Not an official new Scrum Guide edition; the commentary is mixed. Sources: [SensioLabs summary](https://sensiolabs.com/blog/2025/scrum-guide-expansion-pack-2025-key-insights-you-need-to-know), [GitHub repo](https://github.com/ScrumGuides/ScrumGuide-ExpansionPack). Over a year old, so keep as context only. We found no official scrum.org announcement.
- No new Kanban Guide revision could be confirmed (last known update January 2021 for the Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams).

_Web access note: the session could open no resource sites directly (fetch blocked); findings come from web search only, and items a search could not confirm are left out._

## Lessons from our projects
- xo-online: PROJECT.md 'Status' still said 'not published' after release (review F-08). Update the state file in the same commit as the release approval.
- todo-app F-6: the test report said 'CI not yet run' after three green runs. Make the PM stage checklist include 'docs match latest evidence'.
- Both projects needed a second review round; plan the fix and re-review stage into the schedule instead of treating it as a surprise.

## Watch list
- Open scrumguides.org and kanbanguides.org directly to check for any official revision.
- Evaluate whether the Expansion Pack's Product Goal / release guidance helps our single-release flow.
- Atlassian Agile Coach and APM resources: not opened this session.

Learned: the Scrum Guide Expansion Pack (June 2025) is optional and unofficial; core guide unchanged. Will do differently: include 'state file and test report match latest evidence' in every stage's definition of done, and plan a re-review round.

actions.title: Playbook — Imogen Clarke (Graphic Designer)
actions.body:
# Playbook — Imogen Clarke, Senior Graphic Designer & Brand Identity Specialist
Last updated: 2026-11-09

## Standards we follow
- Design the mark to work in one colour, at 16px, and mirrored contexts; deliver SVG with a transparent background and a clear-space rule.
- Bilingual identities: pair Arabic and Latin faces matched for x-height, weight and colour on the line; test Arabic with real words, not lorem ipsum.
- Contrast: WCAG 2.2 AA is the baseline (4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text and UI components); check every colour pair, in light and dark themes.
- Never rely on colour alone to convey meaning (status, errors, overdue); pair with icon or text.
- Check licences: only open-licence fonts (OFL) and assets, since the work is public and costs $0.
- Document tokens (colours, type scale, spacing) in brand guidelines so engineers and the design reviewer can verify them.

## What's new
- **WCAG 3.0 Working Draft, March 2026** (W3C, 2026-03-03): still a draft, not a standard; contrast method (APCA) status is disputed between sources. WCAG 2.2 remains the compliance reference. Sources: [W3C WAI news 2026-03-03](https://www.w3.org/WAI/news/2026-03-03/wcag3), [W3C WCAG 3.0 draft](https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-3.0/). Action: keep using 2.2 AA contrast; do not adopt APCA thresholds.
- **Alexandria** (Google Fonts) is a free variable Arabic and Latin family with nine weights and matched proportions, useful for bilingual identities. Source: [fontalternatives.com](https://fontalternatives.com/fonts/alexandria/) (secondary source; verify on fonts.google.com; no date confirmed, not a new release).
- European Accessibility Act has applied since 2025-06-28; its legal reference is EN 301 549, and sources disagree on whether WCAG 2.1 or 2.2 is formally required, so design to 2.2 AA. Source: [Level Access summary](https://www.levelaccess.com/blog/eaa-compliance-in-2026-how-enforcement-has-evolved-and-what-to-expect-next/) (vendor blog; verify against EUR-Lex).

_Web access note: the session could open no resource sites directly (fetch blocked); findings come from web search only, and items a search could not confirm are left out._

## Lessons from our projects
- xo-online F-06: player names mixing Arabic and Latin broke visually until wrapped in bidi isolation (<bdi>). Brand/type specs should show mixed-direction names and numerals.
- todo-app: overdue state used text plus an icon, not colour alone, and the reviewer verified it in a render. Keep this pattern.
- todo-app F-4: safe-area insets swap in RTL. Any edge-to-edge graphic needs an RTL mock.
- xo-online F-07: reduced-motion behaviour was only checked in Chromium. Specify a static fallback for any animated brand asset.

## Watch list
- Verify Alexandria and other Arabic families on fonts.google.com.
- Track WCAG 3.0 drafts and the EN 301 549 v4 status.
- Open Brand New, Typewolf and Google Fonts Knowledge, not reachable this session.

Learned: WCAG 3.0 is still a March 2026 working draft, so 2.2 AA contrast stays our rule; Alexandria is a matched bilingual variable option. Will do differently: include mixed Arabic/Latin and RTL mock-ups plus reduced-motion fallbacks in specs.
